region: Brooklyn Navy Yard · Brooklyn, New York
about: Kings County Distillery is New York City’s oldest operating whiskey distillery. Colin Spoelman, who grew up in Harlan County in the moonshine country of eastern Kentucky, founded it with David Haskell in 2010 in a tiny space in Williamsburg. It was the first commercial whiskey made in the city since Prohibition. In 2012 the distillery moved into the Paymaster Building, a nineteenth-century brick building inside the Brooklyn Navy Yard that once housed the yard’s paymaster.

The Straight Bourbon uses an unusually high-malt recipe that owes more to Scotch than to Kentucky: 80% organic, non-GMO corn from Lakeview Organic in the Finger Lakes, a farm Kings County has bought from since day one, and 20% Golden Promise malted barley from Thomas Fawcett Maltsters in England. There is no rye or wheat. It is double distilled in true copper pot stills from Forsyths of Scotland and Vendome of Kentucky, aged four to seven years in new charred oak, then blended and bottled at 90 proof.

The distillery’s notes describe maraschino cherry, vanilla bean, fresh coffee and toffee, then raisin, maple syrup, cinnamon and brown sugar, ending on cinnamon sugar and caramel. The malt-heavy recipe gives it more cereal depth and a rounder texture than most bourbons. It has collected medals across the craft-spirits circuit, including a Double Gold at the 2019 San Francisco World Spirits Competition.
